items.title: Conforming Rayleigh–Ritz procedure
items.design_state: Assigned design item; complete current statement and argument are recorded in its item carrier.
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space whose inner product is linear in its first argument. Let $Q\subseteq H$ be a dense linear subspace, and let $q:Q\times Q\to\mathbb C$ be a Hermitian sesquilinear form: it is linear in its first argument, conjugate-linear in its second, and $q(u,v)=\overline{q(v,u)}$ for all $u,v\in Q$. In particular, $q(u,u)\in\mathbb R$. Write $q[u]=q(u,u)$. Assume $q[u]\ge-c\|u\|^2$ for some real $c\ge0$, and assume $Q$ is complete in the form norm $\|u\|_{q,c}^2=q[u]+(c+1)\|u\|^2$; this is the meaning of a closed semibounded form here.

For an integer $n\ge1$, let $\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_n\in Q$ be linearly independent. The exact input matrices are the Gram matrix $G$ and form matrix $A$ with entries

$$G_{ij}=\langle\phi_j,\phi_i\rangle,\qquad A_{ij}=q(\phi_j,\phi_i)\qquad(1\le i,j\le n).$$

For every nonzero coefficient vector $z\in\mathbb C^n$, $z^*Gz=\|\sum_jz_j\phi_j\|^2>0$, so $G$ is positive definite; the symmetry of $q$ makes $A$ Hermitian.

The procedure is:

1. Form $G$ and $A$ from the supplied vectors and form, using exact entries.
2. Diagonalize the positive definite Hermitian matrix $G$ and form its unique positive inverse square root $G^{-1/2}$. Set $B=G^{-1/2}AG^{-1/2}$.
3. Diagonalize the Hermitian matrix $B$, listing its real eigenvalues $\rho_1\le\cdots\le\rho_n$ with multiplicity and selecting an orthonormal eigenbasis $y_1,\ldots,y_n$. For each $j$, set $c_j=G^{-1/2}y_j$ and return $(\rho_j,c_j)$.

Repeated eigenvalues may return any orthonormal basis of the corresponding eigenspace. The procedure uses trial vectors in $Q$ and does not require them to lie in the operator domain of an associated self-adjoint operator. It operates on exact matrix entries: if quadrature or an approximate eigensolver supplies numerical data, this procedure alone supplies no error enclosure or certification for those approximations.

references.title: Phan Thành Nam, Functional Analysis II, lecture notes, Winter 2020–2021, Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München
references.locator: Chapter 2, §2.3, printed pp.17–18: complete min–max treatment for lower-bounded self-adjoint operators. This is independent variational context; the exact matrix procedure is specified locally.

items.proof_route: Define the exact generalized finite Hermitian eigenproblem from the form and Gram matrices; keep quadrature enclosures and numerical solver certification separate, and require no trial vector to lie in D(H).

items.title: Conforming Ritz eigenvalue upper bounds
items.design_state: Assigned design item; complete current statement and argument are recorded in its item carrier.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space, let $A=A^*$ satisfy $A\ge-cI$ for some $c\ge0$, and set $Q(A)=D((A+cI)^{1/2})$. Define the associated closed form by

$$q_A(u,v)=\langle(A+cI)^{1/2}u,(A+cI)^{1/2}v\rangle-c\langle u,v\rangle\qquad(u,v\in Q(A)).$$

Let $\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)$ be the essential spectrum, the complement in $\sigma(A)$ of isolated eigenvalues of finite multiplicity, and put $\alpha=\inf\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)$, with $\alpha=+\infty$ when this set is empty. For $k\ge1$, define

$$\lambda_k(A)=\inf_{\substack{L\subseteq Q(A)\text{ linear},\ \dim L=k}}\ \sup_{\substack{u\in L\\\|u\|=1}}q_A[u],\qquad q_A[u]=q_A(u,u),$$

where the infimum over an empty family is $+\infty$. For a finite-dimensional conforming subspace $V\subseteq Q(A)$ and $1\le k\le\dim V$, define its $k$th Ritz value

$$\theta_k(V)=\inf_{\substack{L\subseteq V\text{ linear},\ \dim L=k}}\ \sup_{\substack{u\in L\\\|u\|=1}}q_A[u].$$

Then $\theta_k(V)\ge\lambda_k(A)$. If $V_1\subseteq V_2\subseteq\cdots\subseteq Q(A)$ are finite-dimensional subspaces whose union is dense in $Q(A)$ in the form norm $\|u\|_{Q(A)}^2=q_A[u]+(c+1)\|u\|^2$, then for every fixed $k$ with $\lambda_k(A)<\alpha$ the values $\theta_k(V_n)$, defined once $\dim V_n\ge k$, decrease to $\lambda_k(A)$, the $k$th isolated eigenvalue below the essential spectrum counted with multiplicity.

references.title: Phan Thành Nam, Functional Analysis II, lecture notes, Winter 2020–2021, Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München
references.locator: Chapter 2, §2.3, printed pp.17–18: min–max characterization, proof, and essential-spectrum threshold. The conforming form-subspace comparison and dense-sequence argument are supplied locally.

items.proof_route: Restrict the global min–max infimum to conforming finite subspaces, then approximate a finite spectral eigenspace in form norm and control its Gram matrix and form matrix uniformly.

items.title: Residual distance and isolated-eigenspace certificate
items.design_state: Assigned design item; complete current statement and argument are recorded in its item carrier.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space and let $T=T^*$ be self-adjoint on $H$, with spectral projection-valued measure $E_T$. Let $u\in D(T)$ satisfy $\|u\|=1$, let $\lambda\in\mathbb R$, and define the residual $r=(T-\lambda I)u$. For a Borel set $\Delta\subseteq\mathbb R$, write $P_\Delta=E_T(\Delta)$. If $g>0$ and $|x-\lambda|\ge g$ for every $x\in\sigma(T)\setminus\Delta$, then

$$\operatorname{dist}(\lambda,\sigma(T))\le\|r\|,\qquad \|(I-P_\Delta)u\|\le\frac{\|r\|}{g},$$

where $\operatorname{dist}(\lambda,S)=\inf_{x\in S}|x-\lambda|$. If $\sigma(T)\setminus\Delta=\varnothing$, the second conclusion is $\|(I-P_\Delta)u\|=0$.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis, ETH Zürich lecture text (2017)
references.locator: Chapter 6 §§6.4–6.5, printed pp.336–351: unbounded functional calculus and spectral PVM. The exact residual distance and selected-cluster inequalities are proved locally.

items.proof_route: Use the scalar PVM norm identity for (T−λ)u; spectral support gives the distance-to-spectrum estimate, and a selected-cluster gap gives the projection bound.

items.title: A posteriori Schrödinger propagation bound
items.design_state: Assigned design item; complete current statement and argument are recorded in its item carrier.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space, let $T=T^*$ be self-adjoint on $H$, and fix $\hbar>0$. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval, let $t_0\in I$, and let $v\in C^1(I;H)$ satisfy $v(s)\in D(T)$ for every $s\in I$ and $s\mapsto Tv(s)$ continuous. Define $r(s)=i\hbar v'(s)-Tv(s)$ and $U_T(t,t_0)=e^{-i(t-t_0)T/\hbar}$ by the Borel functional calculus. Then for every $t\in I$,

$$\|v(t)-U_T(t,t_0)v(t_0)\|\le\frac1\hbar\int_{\min(t,t_0)}^{\max(t,t_0)}\|r(s)\|\,ds.$$

The integral is the ordinary integral of the continuous real-valued function $s\mapsto\|r(s)\|$; the bound is conditional on the stated operator-domain regularity and makes no assertion about an asymptotic approximation outside this residual estimate.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis, ETH Zürich lecture text (2017)
references.locator: Chapter 7, Theorem 7.40 and proof, printed pp.400–401: the unitary group generated by a self-adjoint operator. The residual/Duhamel estimate and its domain regularity are derived locally.

items.proof_route: Differentiate the interaction-picture path using the self-adjoint unitary group on D(T), integrate its continuous residual by the Banach-valued FTC, and use unitarity.

items.title: Hermite Ritz exactness
items.design_state: Assigned design item; complete current statement and argument are recorded in its item carrier.
items.statement: Assume Choice and Countable Choice. Fix $m,\omega,\hbar>0$ and let $H_{\mathrm{osc}}$ be the self-adjoint coefficient-domain realization on $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$ of $-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\frac{d^2}{dx^2}+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}x^2$ with normalized Hermite eigenfunctions $(\psi_j)_{j\ge0}$, where $H_{\mathrm{osc}}\psi_j=E_j\psi_j$ and $E_j=\hbar\omega(j+\frac12)$. For $n\ge1$, let $V_n=\operatorname{span}\{\psi_0,\ldots,\psi_{n-1}\}\subseteq Q(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$. The $n$ Ritz values of the associated form on $V_n$ are exactly $E_0,\ldots,E_{n-1}$ in increasing order, and each continuum residual $(H_{\mathrm{osc}}-E_jI)\psi_j$ is zero.

references.title: James Binney and David Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Cappella Archive (2008; revised printings 2009–2013)
references.locator: Chapter 3 §3.1, printed pp.37–40 (PDF pp.44–47): harmonic-oscillator ladder spectrum and normalized ground state. The exact scaled coefficient-domain realization, completeness and Ritz computation are supplied by local mathematics.

items.proof_route: Use the published coefficient-domain oscillator realization, evaluate its form and Gram matrices on the Hermite eigenbasis, and compute the continuum residuals.

items.title: A small residual does not label an eigenvalue
items.design_state: Assigned design item; complete current statement and argument are recorded in its item carrier.
items.statement: Assume Choice and Countable Choice. The following assertion is false: for every lower-bounded self-adjoint operator $H$ with a lowest eigenvalue $E_0$, every normalized $u\in D(H)$, and every real $\lambda$, if $(H-\lambda I)u=0$, then $\lambda=E_0$ and $u$ belongs to the ground eigenspace $\ker(H-E_0I)$.
items.proof_route: Compute the diagonal two-level spectrum, residual, and ground eigenspace directly.
